name: MA-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+8 district with a long-serving, well-funded incumbent
No public polling; prediction markets price the Democrat near 97%
Milleron's $1.6M haul is notable but she trails badly in cash and shows no outside support
Independent ballot line is a steep hurdle in a Democratic-leaning seat
model.rationale: A Democratic-leaning district, Neal's incumbency and roughly six-to-one cash advantage, and market pricing near 97% all point the same way; Milleron's fundraising signals a serious challenge, but no polling evidence shows the race is close.
model.watch: An independent poll showing Milleron within single digits, or significant outside spending on her behalf, would be the main reason to move this toward Lean D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Nadia Milleron is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
Massachusetts' first district leans Democratic by eight points, and Richard Neal has held the seat since 1989, most recently as a senior figure on the Ways and Means Committee. He enters the general election with a large financial edge, roughly $1.9 million on hand against about $310,000 for Nadia Milleron, an independent who is the principal challenger. No public polls of the race are available, and prediction markets put the Democratic chance near 97 percent.

Milleron has raised an unusual sum for a challenger, about $1.6 million, signaling a genuine effort, but she runs on an independent line in a Democratic-leaning district with no documented outside support. Fundamentals, incumbency, and money all point the same direction, so the seat is rated safe for Democrats, with uncertainty wider than usual because no polling exists.
